text:
incident-bot: Pager triggered — SEV=P1 — streaming endpoints (text/stream) in us-west-2 showing elevated tail latency and stalls. Paging oncall.

kira: i'm paged, looking now. any known deploys in last 12h? :eyes:

mike: i'm taking. seeing p95 ~420ms (usual ~120ms), p99 ~3.4s (usual ~600ms). several streaming sessions show stalled chunks (clients timeout mid-stream).

leo: flagging cache metrics — prefix-cache hit-rate for serving group `us-west-2/stream` dropped to 10% at 23:42 UTC. baseline ~78%.

natalie: that coincides with the prefix-hash rollout yesterday at 23:35 UTC (prefix-hash-v3). can we confirm rollout windows and traffic groups?

mike: checking routing table and recent rollouts...

mike: quick check: `rgctl rollout status prefix-hash-v3 --since 2026-03-14T23:30Z` shows staged to 40% across streaming pool.

leo: dump of cache stats (snippet):
```
prefix-cache: total_keys=12.3M
hit_rate=10.4%  # was 78.6% before rollout
evictions/sec=1200
avg_ttl_ms=240000
```

kira: low hit-rate explains p99 spike — clients hitting cold path/kvstore + paging. any change to salting/namespace?

leo: prefix-v3 changed the salt algorithm (removed legacy salt fallback) -> higher entropy in prefixes, which reduced grouping. results: more unique prefix keys -> lower effective reuse -> hit-rate collapse.

mike: mitigation options: 1) rollback prefix-hash-v3 2) enable legacy-salt-fallback for stream pool 3) increase prefetch window on edge for 10m. i'm going to trigger immediate rollback for streaming routing group.

mike: command: `rgctl rollout rollback prefix-hash-v3 --group us-west-2/stream --force`

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued (job id: rb-20260315-001). Starting...

deploy-bot: Rollback completed successfully at 1764001272.

leo: after rollback: prefix-cache hit-rate climbing -> 62% now, evictions dropping. p99 down to ~820ms, p95 ~180ms. still above baseline but huge improvement.

natalie: customer-impact check: looking at support signals — two customers reported streaming stalls (CS case #20345, #20346). error budget burn estimate: 0.87 of daily error budget for streaming endpoint. tagging customer-success.

kira: good. i'm going to post a brief status to #general: "Mitigation in place (rollback) — metrics improving, investigating root cause; oncall continues monitoring" :thumbsup:

mike: monitoring: keeping prefetch window increased +1 token batch (temporary) to reduce cold fetch pressure. plan: keep watch for 30m, then scale back if stable.

leo: root-cause hypothesis: prefix-hash-v3 increased key entropy, reduced locality for common prefixes used by streaming requests (esp. small prompts). Rollout to a fraction of routing groups amplified cache churn -> paging surge -> tail latency.

natalie: action items assigned: 
- leo: produce a reproducible test that simulates prefix entropy impact on hit-rate (due EOD)
- mike: add a protection rule: block prefix-hash variants unless hit-rate across canary >= 60% for 1h (PR + monitor, due tomorrow)
- kira: coordinate customer comms + incident summary (due today)

mike: handoff: i'm going to stay oncall for 15 more minutes to watch, then handing off to natalie for postmortem/cleanup and customer updates. oncall window ends at 1764002000 for me.

natalie: ack. i'll pick this up — will create postmortem draft and roll-forward plan. also propose a regression test for prefix/cache interaction in the CI harness.

kira: tagging infra-alerts: please add a 1h alert for prefix-cache hit-rate < 40% for any streaming pool; that should catch this earlier.

leo: quick note for follow-ups: consider adding a synthetic streaming workload that exercises small prompt prefix reuse patterns to catch entropy regressions.

mike: final note: incident declared resolved -> mitigation applied (rollback) and metrics recovering. leaving thread open for postmortem notes and customer impact details. :white_check_mark:
